name: Mazdutide
used_for: Once-weekly glucagon and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist discovered by Eli Lilly and developed in China by Innovent. According to a published review (Drugs, 2025), it was approved in China in June 2025 for long-term weight management and in September 2025 for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. It has no FDA approval: no Drugs@FDA or DailyMed product exists, and the only US-registered trials found were Lilly phase 2 studies (obesity, alcohol use disorder). Published phase 3 data come from Chinese adults.

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide 4 mg or 6 mg for 48 weeks.
entries.population: Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (GLORY-1, phase 3)

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide 9 mg for 60 weeks.
entries.population: Chinese adults with obesity, BMI 30 or higher (GLORY-2, phase 3)

entries.text: Once-weekly subcutaneous mazdutide with escalation to 3/6 mg, 10 mg or 16 mg for 48 weeks (starting at 1.5 mg).
entries.population: US adults with obesity or overweight (Lilly phase 2, as registered)

administration_guidance.text: In the GLORY-2 trial, mazdutide was given once weekly by subcutaneous administration alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Mazdutide is investigational and has no label guidance on timing, meals, or storage.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: An educational peptide site says mazdutide injections can be given regardless of meal timing, that an empty stomach or a light meal may reduce discomfort if GI effects occur, that unreconstituted product is kept at 2 to 8 C away from light and not frozen, and that a reconstituted vial is typically used within 14 to 28 days per its labeling. Mazdutide is unapproved in the US, so this is not label guidance.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In GLORY-2 (Chinese adults with obesity), the most common adverse events were vomiting (53.1% vs 1.3% with placebo), nausea (46.9% vs 3.2%), and diarrhea (39.4% vs 6.5%), mostly mild to moderate. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 2.9% with mazdutide vs 0% with placebo.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In GLORY-1, the most frequent adverse events were gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate, and adverse events led to discontinuation in 0.5% to 1.5% of mazdutide recipients and 1.0% of those on placebo.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Superpower, a health testing company, says mazdutide showed about 13 percent placebo-subtracted weight loss at 6 mg in Chinese trials, but that safety data come only from Chinese trials of 32 weeks or less, and that it has no legal pathway for US use.
FormBlends says mazdutide is not FDA-approved or legally available in US pharmacies, cautions that online vendors' product quality is unverifiable, and points US readers to approved drugs.

Peptide Local, an information site, says mazdutide is approved in China but not by the FDA, that a Chinese approval does not carry over to other countries, and cites an FDA warning letter about a seller's mazdutide listing.

research.summary: GLORY-1: phase 3, 48-week trial of mazdutide 4 mg or 6 mg versus placebo in 610 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (N Engl J Med; NCT05607680).
research.finding: Week 48 weight change was -11.0% (4 mg) and -14.0% (6 mg) versus +0.3% with placebo. Gastrointestinal events were most common; 0.5 to 1.5% stopped for adverse events. Results apply to Chinese adults.

research.summary: GLORY-2: phase 3, 60-week trial of mazdutide 9 mg versus placebo in 461 Chinese adults with obesity (JAMA; NCT06164873).
research.finding: Weight change was -16.65% versus -1.50% with placebo. Vomiting (53%), nausea (47%) and diarrhea (39%) were common; 2.9% stopped treatment.

research.summary: 28-week phase 3 trial of mazdutide 4 or 6 mg versus dulaglutide 1.5 mg in 731 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes (Nature; NCT05606913).
research.finding: HbA1c fell more than with dulaglutide (-0.24 and -0.30 points difference) and weight fell more. Gastrointestinal side effects were more frequent than with dulaglutide.

research.summary: 24-week phase 3 trial of mazdutide monotherapy versus placebo in 320 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes (Nature; NCT05628311).
research.finding: HbA1c fell 1.57 (4 mg) and 2.15 (6 mg) points versus 0.14 with placebo; weight fell 5.6 to 7.8% versus 1.3%. Short trial, Chinese participants only.

research.summary: Lilly phase 2 US trial of mazdutide versus placebo for 48 weeks in 179 adults with obesity or overweight.
research.finding: Posted results show week 32 weight change of -7.3% (3/6 mg), -15.6% (10 mg) and -18.1% (16 mg) versus -0.85% with placebo. Only the posted primary outcome table was reviewed; a peer-reviewed paper was not found.

research.summary: Lilly phase 2 US proof-of-concept trial of mazdutide versus placebo in 308 people with alcohol use disorder.
research.finding: Registered as completed in March 2026; no results were posted when reviewed, so there is no verified finding.

research.summary: FDA warning letter dated 31 March 2026 to Prime Sciences.
research.finding: The letter lists mazdutide, among other products, as an unapproved new drug offered for sale for human use despite laboratory-research-only labeling.

research.summary: FDA warning letter dated 10 December 2024 to Xcel Research LLC.
research.finding: The letter lists mazdutide, among other peptides, as an unapproved new drug sold with research-use-only labels.

research.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial of once-weekly mazdutide escalated to 16 mg for 20 weeks in 32 adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes, 24 on mazdutide and 8 on placebo (Bhattachar et al., Diabetes Obes Metab; NCT05623839).
research.finding: Weight fell 20.0% and 21.0% in the two escalation cohorts versus 0.1% with placebo at week 20. No serious adverse events were reported and the most common events were mild or moderate gastrointestinal disorders. Small, short trial.

research.summary: Randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b multiple-ascending-dose trial of once-weekly mazdutide in 24 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity, escalating every 4 weeks to 9 mg over 12 weeks or to 10 mg over 16 weeks (Ji et al., EClinicalMedicine; NCT04440345).
research.finding: Weight fell 11.7% (9 mg, 12 weeks) versus 1.8% with placebo and 9.5% (10 mg, 16 weeks) versus 3.3%. No serious adverse events; all events were mild or moderate, most often upper respiratory infection, diarrhea, decreased appetite and nausea.

research.summary: Narrative review of the cardiovascular effects of glucagon receptor signaling alone and with GLP-1 receptor signaling in dual agonists such as mazdutide and survodutide (Kushner, Michos et al., J Am Heart Assoc).
research.finding: Glucagon is described as regulating energy balance, lipid metabolism and glucose. Dual agonists including mazdutide increased heart rate to a similar extent as GLP-1 only drugs and also lowered blood pressure and blood sugar. One other dual agonist was stopped partly over large heart rate rises and QT prolongation.

dose.summary: In phase 3 trials in Chinese adults, mazdutide was given as 4 mg or 6 mg once weekly for 48 weeks, or 9 mg once weekly for 60 weeks. Smaller trials escalated in steps of about 4 weeks up to 9, 10 or 16 mg. Online sites describe 1 to 9 mg schedules that vary from the trials, and none are from an FDA label because mazdutide has none.

items.text: Peptide Initiative, an educational peptide site, suggests 1.5 mg to 6 mg once weekly, starting at 1.5 mg to limit stomach effects, then moving to 4 mg or 6 mg.

items.text: Doctronic, a health information site, says trials began at 1 mg once weekly and rose about every 4 weeks through 2, 3 and 4 mg, with some arms reaching 6 mg, so reaching 4 to 6 mg could take roughly 12 to 20 weeks.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Schedule, an educational site, lists 3 mg weekly for weeks 1 to 4, 6 mg for weeks 5 to 16 and 9 mg from week 17. This schedule is not one of the published trial schedules.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: No study reviewed reports a best time of day for mazdutide. Online sites advise injecting on the same day and at a similar time each week.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says to give mazdutide at the same time each week.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Schedule says to inject once weekly on the same day each week at a consistent time.
items.label: internet

fasting.summary: In the GLORY-2 trial mazdutide was given with a reduced-calorie diet and more activity. In type 2 diabetes trials it lowered blood sugar. Online sites say meal timing does not matter, and one says an empty stomach or a light meal may ease stomach upset, which has not been tested.

items.text: In the GLORY-2 trial, mazdutide was given once weekly alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Mazdutide is investigational and has no label guidance on meals.
items.label: research

items.text: In a 24-week phase 3 trial in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, mazdutide lowered HbA1c, a measure of average blood sugar, by 1.57 points (4 mg) and 2.15 points (6 mg) versus 0.14 with placebo.
items.label: research

items.label: internet

frequency.summary: Every mazdutide trial reviewed used one injection per week. No missed-dose rule or rule for changing the injection day was found, because there is no US label. Online sites repeat the once-weekly schedule.

items.text: In the GLORY-2 trial, mazdutide was given once weekly by subcutaneous injection.
items.label: research

items.label: research

items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Published phase 3 trials ran 48 and 60 weeks, and no data were found on weight after stopping mazdutide. Online sites call it long-term treatment and warn that longer safety data are lacking.

items.text: GLORY-1 lasted 48 weeks and GLORY-2 lasted 60 weeks, giving mazdutide once weekly to Chinese adults. Neither abstract reports what happened after stopping.
items.label: research

items.text: A phase 1 trial gave mazdutide for 20 weeks in 32 adults and a phase 1b trial for 12 or 16 weeks in 24 adults, which is far shorter than the phase 3 trials.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Initiative describes the cycle length as ongoing with no fixed end.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Schedule says mazdutide is used as continuous long-term therapy with no cycling protocol studied, and that weight regain is expected after stopping. It gives no study for the regain claim.
items.label: internet

items.text: Superpower, a health testing company, says the longest published phase 3 trial ran 60 weeks and that longer-term safety has not been studied in published trials. It reports no data on weight regain after stopping.
items.label: internet

storage_and_handling.summary: Mazdutide has no US label, so no storage rules are published by a regulator. Two online sites say to keep unmixed product at 2 to 8 C away from light and to use a mixed vial within a few weeks.

items.text: Peptide Initiative says unreconstituted product is kept at 2 to 8 C, protected from light and moisture, and not frozen. It says a reconstituted vial is kept refrigerated and typically used within 14 to 28 days per its labeling, and to discard it if cloudy, discolored, frozen or expired.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Initiative says to inject into fatty tissue such as the abdomen (at least 2 inches from the belly button), front of the thighs or back of the upper arms.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Schedule says to store lyophilized (freeze-dried) powder at 2 to 8 C, refrigerate after reconstitution and use within 4 weeks, and discard if cloudy or containing particles.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Schedule says to rotate between the abdomen, thigh and upper arm and not inject the same spot twice in a row.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: Mazdutide is a once-weekly drug that activates two receptors, GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) and glucagon. The GLP-1 part lowers appetite, and the glucagon part is thought to raise energy burned, though this is described as emerging evidence in people.

items.text: A review says glucagon receptor signaling regulates energy balance, lipid metabolism and glucose, and that drugs activating both the glucagon and GLP-1 receptors, such as mazdutide, may add efficacy to GLP-1 only drugs. It notes evidence that the glucagon receptor is expressed in the human heart is lacking.
items.label: research

items.text: Superpower says mazdutide combines appetite suppression through the GLP-1 receptor with higher energy expenditure through the glucagon receptor, driving heat production and fat burning in brown fat and liver.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: In GLORY-2, 9 mg weekly cut body weight by 16.7% over 60 weeks versus 1.5% with placebo in Chinese adults with obesity. In GLORY-1, 6 mg cut it by 14.0% at 48 weeks versus a 0.3% gain on placebo.

items.text: GLORY-2: mean body weight change at week 60 was -16.65% with mazdutide 9 mg versus -1.50% with placebo in 461 Chinese adults with obesity, and 84.3% lost 5% or more versus 33.1%.
items.label: research

items.text: GLORY-1: at week 48 mean weight change was -11.00% (4 mg) and -14.01% (6 mg) versus +0.30% with placebo in 610 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity.
items.label: research

items.text: In adults with type 2 diabetes, 24 weeks of mazdutide lowered HbA1c by 1.57 (4 mg) to 2.15 (6 mg) points versus 0.14 with placebo, with 5.6 to 7.8% weight loss.
items.label: research

items.text: Superpower says placebo-subtracted weight loss at week 32 was about 10.5% at 4 mg and 13.0% at 6 mg.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Common
side_effect_groups.summary: Stomach and gut effects were the most common in phase 3 trials: vomiting (53%), nausea (47%) and diarrhea (39%) at 9 mg. Most were mild or moderate and few people stopped treatment.

items.text: In GLORY-2 (Chinese adults with obesity), the most common adverse events were vomiting (53.1% vs 1.3% with placebo), nausea (46.9% vs 3.2%), and diarrhea (39.4% vs 6.5%), mostly mild to moderate. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 2.9% with mazdutide vs 0% with placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: In GLORY-1, the most frequent adverse events were gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate, and adverse events led to discontinuation in 0.5% to 1.5% of mazdutide recipients and 1.0% of those on placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Initiative says the most frequent effects are nausea, diarrhea and decreased appetite, with vomiting and injection site reactions less common.
items.label: internet

items.text: FormBlends, a compounded-peptide seller, says nausea, diarrhea and vomiting were most common and concentrated in the titration (dose-raising) phase.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: At higher doses
side_effect_groups.summary: Small early trials up to 16 mg reported no serious adverse events. Two online sites say about 20 percent stopped at the 16 mg dose in US studies, which was not confirmed here.

items.text: In a phase 1 trial of mazdutide up to 16 mg for 20 weeks in 32 adults, no serious adverse events were reported and the most common events were mild or moderate gastrointestinal disorders.
items.label: research

items.text: In a phase 1b trial of 9 mg and 10 mg doses in 24 Chinese adults, no serious adverse events were reported, and the most common events were upper respiratory infection, diarrhea, decreased appetite and nausea.
items.label: research

items.text: FormBlends, a compounded-peptide seller, says discontinuation was 0.5 to 1.5% at approved doses but reached 20 percent at the highest 16 mg dose in US studies.
items.label: internet

items.text: Superpower says nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are dose dependent and that one trial reported 20% stopping the 16 mg dose because of adverse events.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Heart rate
side_effect_groups.summary: A review found mazdutide raised heart rate about as much as GLP-1 only drugs while lowering blood pressure. Another dual agonist was stopped partly over large heart rate rises.

items.text: A review says dual glucagon and GLP-1 receptor agonists including mazdutide increased heart rate to a similar extent as GLP-1 only drugs, and also reduced blood pressure and blood sugar. At least one other dual agonist was stopped partly because of large heart rate increases and QT prolongation.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Long-term safety
side_effect_groups.summary: Published safety data stop at 60 weeks and come from Chinese adults, so effects of longer use are unknown.

items.text: Superpower says all phase 3 safety data come from Chinese populations in published trials lasting up to 60 weeks, and that longer-term safety has not been studied in published trials.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Regulator warning
side_effect_groups.summary: Mazdutide is approved in China but not by the FDA. The FDA has warned sellers that mazdutide sold online is an unapproved new drug.

items.text: A 31 March 2026 FDA warning letter to Prime Sciences lists mazdutide, among other products, as an unapproved new drug offered for sale for human use despite laboratory-research-only labeling.
items.label: research

items.text: A 10 December 2024 FDA warning letter to Xcel Research LLC lists mazdutide, among other peptides, as an unapproved new drug sold with research-use-only labels.
items.label: research

items.text: Superpower says mazdutide is not legally available for human use in the United States and that there is no legal pathway to obtain pharmaceutical-grade mazdutide for human use in the US as of September 2026.
items.label: internet

items.text: FormBlends, a compounded-peptide seller, says mazdutide is not FDA-approved or legally available in US pharmacies, that buyers cannot verify online vendors' product is the molecule used in trials, and that approved options such as Wegovy and Zepbound are the legitimate paths.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Local, an information site, says mazdutide is approved in China but not by the FDA and that a March 2026 FDA warning letter named one seller's mazdutide listing as an unapproved new drug.
items.label: internet
